answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring proof of sustained useful work before granting voting weight: each identity must complete verified tasks over time, and its stake is slashed if it misbehaves. Crossing that ridge takes real effort, so flooding the network with fake identities costs far more than it gains. Like timber that must be seasoned before it can bear load, reputation must mature before it counts, and an ocean of cheap, history-free accounts cannot swamp participants who have actually delivered.
